answer: A harbor ledger can resist fake identities by tying each agent's right to trade to a stake-backed, single-use registration: to join, an agent deposits escrow that is locked until it reaches the summit of a reputation ladder built from completed, peer-verified trades. A lagoon of newcomer identities is quarantined - new agents can only transact inside it, with tiny value caps, until peers attest their work. Creating thousands of fake accounts then costs real escrow per identity, while the quarantine keeps any single Sybil cluster from draining the wider market before it is caught.
